Week of November 16, 2026

Denver Conference Previews the 2028 Field as Shapiro Steps Forward and Van Hollen Steps Aside

Ten days after the midterms, would-be 2028 candidates tested their messages at the What's Next conference in Denver on November 13. Gov. Josh Shapiro, whom CNN describes as expected to run, gave a campaign-style speech and said he would be doing his part. Sen. Elissa Slotkin said she is seriously considering a run, Sen. Cory Booker said he is giving it hard thought, and Rep. Ro Khanna said the reception made him more likely to consider it. Nobody has formally declared.

Sen. Chris Van Hollen, who had previously expressed interest in a presidential run, told reporters he is not running in 2028 and is instead challenging Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader in a December 1 vote. Pete Buttigieg said he would have no news on 2028 anytime soon, and Sen. Ruben Gallego said his three young children weigh heavily on his decision.

Odds moves are small this week. Shapiro rises a point on his post-election momentum, and Gallego slips a point. We add Booker and Slotkin to the board, moving their chances out of the unlisted field, which falls from 18 to 15 percent. Ossoff won a straw poll of 990 activists at Crooked Media's conference on November 7 and still leads prediction markets near 27 percent, but he says he is not running, so we hold him at 8. A CNN/SSRS poll taken before the midterms found Democrats about equally excited by Harris, Ocasio-Cortez and Buttigieg.
